nodes.title: Tyrosine supply
nodes.short: The starting material, from the blood.
nodes.what: Tyrosine, an amino acid, is the starting material for dopamine. It comes from protein in food, and the body can also make it from another amino acid, phenylalanine, using the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH).

adhd.text: No established link (GEN-03). Phenylketonuria (PKU), where PAH does not work, is a separate condition.

nodes.limits: This map is not diet advice. It does not show that eating more protein or taking tyrosine changes ADHD symptoms.

refs.quote: phenylalanine hydroxylase that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine

nodes.title: Entry into the brain
nodes.what: To reach brain nerve cells, tyrosine has to cross the blood–brain barrier. It uses LAT1 (gene SLC7A5), a carrier for large neutral amino acids, and competes for it with other amino acids of that type, such as phenylalanine.
nodes.limits: The LAT1 statement comes from the discussion section of a rat and mouse study and describes the transporter's general role.

refs.quote: LAT1 is a high affinity amino acid transporter that accounts for the uptake of large neutral amino acids into the brain

refs.loc: Biochemical markers for assessment of metabolic control; Functional effect of Phe-free L-amino acid supplements
refs.quote: Phe and Tyr compete to cross the blood–brain barrier … LNAA block the transport of Phe across the blood brain barrier

nodes.title: Tyrosine to L-DOPA
nodes.what: The enzyme tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) converts tyrosine to L-DOPA. It is the rate-limiting step: the slowest, most tightly controlled step in making dopamine and the other catecholamines.
nodes.needs: BH4 (tetrahydrobiopterin), oxygen, and iron held in the enzyme.

adhd.text: None established (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists TH within 50 kb (GEN-12).

nodes.medicines: Levodopa, used mainly for Parkinson's disease, supplies L-DOPA directly and so does not depend on this step (GEN-03).
nodes.limits: “Rate-limiting” describes how much dopamine is made. How strongly dopamine signals also depends on packaging, release, receptors and clearance.

refs.quote: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting enzyme of catecholamine biosynthesis; it uses tetrahydrobiopterin and molecular oxygen to convert tyrosine to DOPA.
it must be in the ferrous state to carry out catalysis

nodes.title: L-DOPA to dopamine
nodes.what: The enzyme aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC, gene DDC) converts L-DOPA to dopamine.
nodes.needs: PLP (pyridoxal phosphate), the active form of vitamin B6.

adhd.text: None established (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists DDC within 50 kb (GEN-12).

nodes.limits: AADC deficiency is a rare inherited condition. It is mentioned to show that this step matters, not as an explanation of ADHD.

refs.quote: after decarboxylation to dopamine is transferred into the synaptic vesicle
a rare, autosomal recessive neurometabolic disorder … secondary failure of AADC due to a deficiency of its cofactor pyridoxal phosphate (PLP)

nodes.title: Packaging into vesicles
nodes.short: Loaded into storage sacs by VMAT2.
nodes.what: VMAT2 (gene SLC18A2) loads dopamine from inside the cell into vesicles, the small sacs that store it ready for release.
nodes.needs: A proton gradient across the vesicle wall, built by the vesicle's proton pump.

adhd.text: One small platelet study (GEN-03 rates this Tier C). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists SLC18A2 within 50 kb (GEN-12).

nodes.medicines: Amphetamine inhibits VMAT2, which releases dopamine from vesicle storage. Methylphenidate is reported to redistribute VMAT2.
nodes.limits: After release, vesicles are recycled and refilled; that cycle is not drawn as a separate step.

refs.quote: DAT and … VMAT-2, which transport DA into presynaptic terminals and synaptic vesicles, respectively
increases vesicular DA release via inhibition of the vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT-2) … redistribution of VMAT-2
vesicles are recycled, refilled with neurotransmitters, and reused for release

nodes.title: Release
nodes.short: Calcium triggers vesicles to release dopamine.
nodes.what: When an electrical signal reaches the nerve ending, calcium flows in and triggers vesicles to fuse with the cell membrane, releasing dopamine into the gap between cells.

adhd.text: No specific link stated on this site.

nodes.medicines: Amphetamine can also move dopamine out of the cell by making the transporter DAT run in reverse (see Reuptake).
nodes.limits: Release is adjusted moment to moment by the cell's activity and by autoreceptor feedback.

refs.quote: Ca2+ entering a presynaptic terminal triggers synaptic vesicle exocytosis and neurotransmitter release in less than a millisecond

nodes.title: BH4 helper molecule
nodes.what: Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) is a helper molecule (cofactor) that tyrosine hydroxylase needs. BH4 has its own rate-limiting step, made by the enzyme GTP cyclohydrolase I (GCH1).

adhd.text: None established. GCH1 conditions are movement disorders (see GEN-06).

nodes.limits: A support link, not a step in the sequence.

refs.quote: uses tetrahydrobiopterin and molecular oxygen to convert tyrosine to DOPA

refs.loc: 3.3 PP2A, AADC, GTP cyclohydrolase, VMAT, DJ-1
refs.quote: GTP cyclohydrolase (GTPCH), the rate-limiting enzyme of tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis

nodes.title: Vitamin B6 (PLP)
nodes.what: Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP), the active form of vitamin B6, is the cofactor AADC needs to convert L-DOPA to dopamine.
nodes.limits: A support link, not a step. This map does not give supplement advice.

refs.quote: secondary failure of AADC due to a deficiency of its cofactor pyridoxal phosphate (PLP)

nodes.title: Vesicle proton pump
nodes.what: A pump in the vesicle wall, the vesicular proton ATPase (V-ATPase), uses ATP to push protons into the vesicle, making it acidic and charged inside. Vesicle transporters, including VMAT2, use this gradient to load their transmitter.
nodes.limits: The pump is not driven directly by the mitochondria's own proton gradient; energy supply matters through ATP (GEN-03).

refs.quote: all VNTs rely on the vesicular VoATPase that pumps H+ ions into the SV and builds up an electrochemical gradient

nodes.title: Energy (ATP)
nodes.what: ATP is the cell's energy currency. The vesicle's proton pump is an ATPase: it uses ATP to do its work.
nodes.limits: This is not a measure of anyone's energy, tiredness or “battery level”.

refs.quote: an electrochemical gradient ΔμH+ driven by the proton ATPase

nodes.title: Receptors
nodes.short: Dopamine binds receptors on nearby cells.
nodes.what: Released dopamine binds dopamine receptors on nearby cells. There are five types, D1 to D5, grouped as D1-like (D1 and D5) and D2-like (D2, D3 and D4).

adhd.text: Older candidate-gene studies reported signals for DRD4 and DRD5, with heterogeneity, before genome-wide studies (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists DRD4 or DRD5 within 50 kb.

nodes.medicines: Some medicines act directly on dopamine receptors, such as drugs for Parkinson's disease and antipsychotics.
nodes.limits: Receptor signalling inside the receiving cell is not drawn.

refs.loc: Dopamine D2-autoreceptors – Location and Behavioral Function
refs.quote: The five mammalian receptor subtypes are divided into two major groups that form the D1-like (D1 and D5) and D2-like (D2, D3, and D4) receptors.
multiple pharmacologically active compounds that directly target dopamine receptors, such as antiparkinson drugs and antipsychotics
candidate-gene signals for DRD4 and DRD5
nearby genes within 50 kb of index variants

nodes.title: Reuptake
nodes.short: DAT carries dopamine back into the cell.
nodes.what: After release, the dopamine transporter (DAT, gene SLC6A3) carries dopamine back into the releasing cell. In the striatum this is the main way released dopamine is cleared. In the frontal cortex DAT is sparse: mouse studies found that dopamine there is taken up mainly by the noradrenaline transporter (NET, gene SLC6A2).

adhd.text: Candidate-gene signal for DAT1 (SLC6A3), with heterogeneity (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists SLC6A3 within 50 kb (GEN-12).

nodes.medicines: Methylphenidate inhibits DAT and NET. Amphetamine also inhibits these transporters and can make DAT run in reverse, moving dopamine out of the cell.
nodes.limits: The frontal-cortex finding comes from mouse studies; how closely it applies to people is less certain. How much dopamine taken back up is reused is not drawn, because it was not separately source-checked.

refs.quote: clearance of dopamine from the extracellular space is primarily determined by uptake by the dopamine transporter (DAT)
whereas dopamine uptake in caudate and nucleus accumbens depends primarily on the DAT, dopamine uptake in frontal cortex depends primarily on the NET
The direct effects of MPH include inhibition of the DAT and NET … release of cytosolic DA via reverse transport by the DAT
candidate-gene signal for DAT1

nodes.title: Breakdown
nodes.short: MAO and COMT break dopamine down.
nodes.what: Dopamine is broken down by two enzyme families, monoamine oxidase (MAO) and catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT). In the mouse frontal cortex, COMT accounts for about half of dopamine clearance.

adhd.text: No ADHD link is stated for MAO or COMT on GEN-03. None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists COMT, MAOA or MAOB within 50 kb.

nodes.medicines: Amphetamine is reported to inhibit monoamine oxidase activity.
nodes.limits: The regional figure comes from a mouse study.

refs.quote: in the mouse, PFC COMT contributes about one half of the total DA clearance
monoamine oxidase activity inhibition

nodes.title: Autoreceptor feedback
nodes.short: A brake on the releasing cell.
nodes.what: Some released dopamine binds D2-type autoreceptors on the releasing cell itself. They act as a brake: feedback that controls the cell's firing and how much dopamine it makes, releases and takes back up.

adhd.text: No specific link stated on this site.

nodes.limits: Feedback keeps the system within a working range. It is not a fixed personal set-point.

refs.quote: providing feedback inhibition that controls cell firing and the synthesis, release, and uptake of dopamine

nodes.title: Noradrenaline branch
nodes.short: One extra step in noradrenaline cells.
nodes.what: In noradrenaline-releasing nerve cells there is one extra step. Inside vesicles, the enzyme dopamine β-hydroxylase (DBH) converts dopamine to noradrenaline. This happens in the brain, in nerves elsewhere in the body, and in the adrenal gland.

adhd.text: ADHD stimulant medicines act on the noradrenaline transporter (NET) as well as DAT.

nodes.medicines: Methylphenidate and amphetamine both inhibit NET.
nodes.limits: Shown for context. This page does not map the noradrenaline system in detail. DBH's own cofactors are not listed because they were not source-checked for this page.

refs.quote: (nor)adrenergic neurosecretory vesicles in the central and peripheral nervous system … where the enzyme DBH … converts dopamine to norepinephrine
Catecholamine synthesis then continues in vesicles via the actions of dopamine-β-hydroxylase
dopamine and norepinephrine transporter inhibition

nodes.title: Outside the brain
nodes.what: Tyrosine hydroxylase also works outside the brain, for example in the adrenal gland, which makes adrenaline. Levodopa taken as a medicine is mostly broken down in the body before it reaches the brain, mainly by AADC, so it is given with a peripheral AADC inhibitor such as carbidopa or benserazide.

adhd.text: Not an ADHD finding; shown so that the brain line is not read as a universal rule.

nodes.medicines: Carbidopa and benserazide block AADC outside the brain so that more levodopa reaches it.
nodes.limits: “Entry into the brain, then conversion” is the order for brain dopamine cells only, not for the adrenal gland or other nerves.
